text_en: The RMS Queen Mary 2, at the time the largest ocean liner ever built, is christened by its namesake's granddaughter, Queen Elizabeth II.
Bartholomew I of Constantinople visits Cuba.
NASA's Opportunity rover lands on the surface of Mars.
The Rotterdam Convention comes into force.
Haitian president Jean-Bertrand Aristide is overthrown in a coup d'état.
NASA releases the Hubble Ultra-Deep Field image of early galaxies.
Al-Qaeda bombings on Cercanías trains in Madrid, Spain, kill at least 192 people.
Vladimir Putin is reelected president of Russia with 71.2 percent of the vote.
Ethnic violence breaks out in Kosovo between Albanians and Serbs.
Hamas leader Ahmed Yassin is killed by Israeli missile strikes.

Bombings attributed to the Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan kill 15 in Tashkent, the capital of Uzbekistan. This is the first instance of suicide bombings in the country or the surrounding region of central Asia.
Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Slovakia and Slovenia are admitted to NATO, the largest expansion of the organization.
The Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) abducts over 1,000 people from the Bajura District to fight in the Nepalese Civil War.
The Humanitarian Ceasefire Agreement is signed by the Sudanese government and two rebel groups to create a ceasefire in the War in Darfur.
A newborn western gorilla is observed for the first time in 50 years in the Léfini Faunal Reserve.
Poland bans the use of chlorofluorocarbons.
Israeli helicopters fire missiles at a convoy of vehicles in the Gaza Strip, killing Hamas leader Abdel Aziz al-Rantisi.
Newly elected prime minister of Spain, José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, announces the withdrawal of all 1,300 Spanish troops from Iraq.
Russia launches the Soyuz TMA-4 mission.
Ukrainian boxer Vitali Klitschko becomes the WBC world heavyweight champion after defeating his opponent Corrie Sanders.
The Gherkin opens in London.
Patriarch Bartholomew I of Constantinople breaks Eucharistic communion with Archbishop Christodoulos of Athens.
The European Union expands by 10 new member states: Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Slovakia, and Slovenia.
Garçon à la pipe, painted by Pablo Picasso in 1905, is sold for $104.2 million. This was the highest price a work of art had ever been sold for at auction.
A stadium bombing in Grozny, Chechnya, Russia kills ten people, including regional governor Akhmad Kadyrov.
15 – The Eurovision Song Contest 2004 takes place in Istanbul, Turkey, and is won by Ukrainian entrant Ruslana with the song "Wild Dances".
The Ralito II Agreement is signed between Colombia and the United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia.
The Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants enters into force.
Manmohan Singh, a Sikh, is sworn in as India's first non-Hindu prime minister.
The Seattle Central Library opens in Seattle, Washington.
A fire at a Momart warehouse destroys numerous works of art.
The United Nations Stabilisation Mission in Haiti (MINUSTAH) peacekeeping mission begins in Haiti.
A transit of Venus occurs.
In Mojave, California, United States, SpaceShipOne becomes the first privately funded spaceplane to achieve spaceflight.
The International Criminal Court opens an investigation into crimes against humanity during the Second Congo War.
The US-led coalition occupying Iraq, the Coalition Provisional Authority (CPA), transfers sovereignty to the Iraqi Interim Government.
The International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture enters into force.
The International Court of Justice issues an advisory ruling that the construction of the West Bank barrier violates the Palestinian people's right to self-determination.
The use of magnetic resonance imaging to study the spin of a single electron is reported.
The Mexican government files charges against former President of Mexico Luis Echeverría for his role in the 1971 Corpus Christi massacre.
The International Criminal Court opens an investigation into the actions of the Lord's Resistance Army in Uganda.
The Frauenkirche church finishes reconstruction after its destruction in 1945.
NASA's MESSENGER space probe is launched, with its primary mission being the study of Mercury.
13 – Typhoon Rananim causes widespread destruction as it strikes China.
Fighting breaks out in the Georgian–Ossetian conflict.
The Rio–Antirrio Bridge opens in Greece.
29 – The 2004 Summer Olympics are held in Athens, Greece.
Google makes its initial public offering.
Armed robbers steal Edvard Munch's The Scream, Madonna, and other paintings from the Munch Museum in Oslo, Norway.
Two Russian passenger jets are downed by suicide bombers during the Second Chechen War.
The immunity of former Chilean dictator Augusto Pinochet is revoked so he can be charged with crimes against humanity.
Former Yugoslavian president Slobodan Milošević stands trial for crimes against humanity.
Chechen rebels take 1,128 hostages, mostly children, at a school in Beslan, Russia. Russian security forces eventually storm the building, resulting in more than 330 people being killed.
A fire breaks out at the Duchess Anna Amalia Library.

In the AFL finals, Essendon defeated Melbourne by five points (15.14.104 - 15.9.99) in the elimination final at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. The victory would prove to be Essendon's most recent finals win, beginning a finals drought that would extend for more than two decades.
Fijian golfer Vijay Singh unseats Tiger Woods as the top PGA Tour player.
The Scottish Parliament Building opens.
The Genesis space probe crash-lands in Utah after a three-year study of the Sun.
An explosion in Ryanggang Province, North Korea, prompts suspicion that North Korea is testing nuclear weapons.
Patriarch Peter VII of Alexandria is killed in a helicopter crash.
Hurricane Jeanne hits the island of Hispaniola, killing thousands in the Dominican Republic and Haiti.
Suicide bombers detonate two bombs at the Red Sea resort of Taba, Egypt, killing 34 people and injuring 171, mostly Israeli tourists.
Afghanistan holds its first presidential election. Hamid Karzai wins with 55.4 percent of the vote.
Russia launches the Soyuz TMA-5 mission.
The prehistoric human species Homo floresiensis is described.
George W. Bush is reelected president of the United States, defeating his challenger John Kerry.
Conflict resumes in the First Ivorian Civil War as fighting breaks out between rebels and French peacekeepers.
Russia ratifies the Kyoto Protocol.
The Second Battle of Fallujah begins in Fallujah, Iraq.
Mozilla releases the Firefox browser.
Palestinian president Yasser Arafat dies. Mahmoud Abbas is appointed as his successor.
The European Space Agency probe SMART-1 arrives at the Moon, becoming the first European satellite to fly to the Moon and orbit it.
26 – Typhoon Muifa kills 600 people in the Philippines.
Nintendo releases the Nintendo DS handheld game console in North America.

The Orange Revolution begins, following a disputed presidential election in Ukraine where Viktor Yanukovych won against Viktor Yushchenko amid accusations of electoral fraud. A revote results in Yushchenko being declared the winner.
December 3 – Typhoon Nanmadol kills 775 people in the Philippines.
EUFOR takes over peacekeeping duties in Bosnia and Herzegovina from the United Nations.
The world's tallest bridge, the Millau Viaduct over the Tarn in the Massif Central mountains, France, is inaugurated.
Iraqi insurgents attack a U.S. military base in the city of Mosul, killing 22 people.

The 9.1–9.3 Mw Indian Ocean earthquake shakes northern Sumatra with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent). One of the largest observed tsunamis follows, affecting coastal areas of Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, Somalia, the Maldives, Malaysia, Myanmar, Bangladesh, and Indonesia, killing 227,000 people.
A peace agreement is reached between Senegal and the Movement of Democratic Forces of Casamance.
